rules.h1sub: card game rules & how to play

sub: Four cards face down, one quick peek, and from then on it's all memory. A hostel favourite that takes two minutes to learn.
goal: The goal: have the lowest total in your cards when the round ends. You hardly ever see them, so remember what you peeked at, swap out high cards and keep an eye on everyone else.

seo.rulesD: How to play Cambio with a normal deck: dealing, card values, card powers, stacking, calling Cambio and scoring – short and clear.

info.gearAlt: A deck of 52 playing cards plus two jokers
info.intro: Cambio is the faster, more chaotic cousin of Cabo: four face-down cards, special powers to peek and swap, and quick-reaction stacking whenever a matching card hits the pile. Two minutes to learn, impossible to stop after one round.

setup.lead: You need a normal deck of 52 cards plus the two jokers, and 2 to 6 players. For more players, shuffle in a second deck.
setup.alt: Four cards lie face down in a square. The two cards nearest to the player are peeked at once.
setup.s1p: Everyone gets 4 cards face down and lays them out in a 2 × 2 square in front of them. Don't look yet.
setup.s2p: Look at the two cards nearest to you, remember them and put them back in exactly the same place. After that your cards stay face down.
setup.s3p: The rest of the deck goes face down in the middle as the draw pile. Turn over its top card to start the discard pile.

values.lead: At the end, each card counts for points. Low is good. Suits don't matter, except for the kings.
values.p: So the red king is the best card in the game, followed by the joker. Black kings, queens and jacks are the ones you want to get rid of.

turn.startP: Whoever won the last round, or simply the player left of the dealer. Play then goes clockwise.
turn.dq: Draw the top card of the draw pile.
turn.dqs: Only you look at it. Then decide:
turn.keepP: Swap it for one of your face-down cards. The card you take out goes face up on the discard pile. Its power does not count.
turn.dropP: Put it straight on the discard pile. If it has a power, you may use it now.
turn.next: Then it's the next player's turn.
turn.memo: You may not rearrange your cards or look at them without a power. Swapped cards go exactly where the old card was, so you can keep track of every spot.

powers.lead: Some cards do something when you draw them and throw them away right away. Using the power is up to you.
powers.peekP: Look at one of your own cards, then put it back.
powers.spyP: Look at one card of another player. They don't get to see it.
powers.blindP: Swap one of your cards with a card of another player – without looking at either.
powers.lookP: Look at one of your cards and one card of another player. Then decide whether to swap the two.
powers.note: A card you swapped out of your square never has a power. The red king has none either – it is simply worth −1.

stacking.lead: This is where Cambio gets fast. As soon as a card lands on the discard pile, anyone may throw a card of the same rank on top – even when it isn't their turn.
stacking.alt: A 6 of clubs lies on the discard pile. A 6 of hearts from a hand is put on top.
stacking.own: Your own card: it goes on the pile and you have one card fewer. Fewer cards, fewer points.
stacking.other: Someone else's card: if you know another player's card matches, throw it on the pile. Then give them one of your cards, face down and without looking, into the empty spot.
stacking.wrong: Wrong card: it goes back where it was, and you draw a penalty card face down from the draw pile and add it to your cards.
stacking.p: Only the rank counts: any 6 matches any 6. Only the first player to stack on a card gets it; always one card at a time, and you may only touch cards with one hand. Stacked cards never trigger a power. Once the next player draws, the chance is gone.

cambio.lead: Think you have the lowest total? Then call it – but only at the start of your turn, instead of drawing.
cambio.s1p: You don't draw. From now on your cards are locked: nobody may swap them, look at them or stack them.
cambio.s2p: Every other player gets exactly one more turn, in the usual order. Stacking still works.
cambio.s3p: All players turn over their cards and add up the points. The lowest total wins the round.
cambio.tieP: If the caller ties with someone, the other player wins – calling is a risk. If it is still a draw, the player with fewer cards wins.
cambio.emptyP: Keep the top card of the discard pile, shuffle the rest and use it as the new draw pile. A player who has no cards left stays in the round and scores 0.

scoring.lead: After every round, everyone writes down the total of their own cards.
scoring.alt: Example: ace, 3, red king and 7 make 1 + 3 − 1 + 7 = 10 points.
scoring.p: Play as many rounds as you like, or until someone goes over 100 points. Then the player with the lowest overall score wins. For a short game, a single round is enough.

varLead: Cambio is passed on by word of mouth, so every table plays it a little differently. Agree on these points before you start:
var1: Taking from the discard pile: some groups let you take the top discard instead of drawing. You must then swap it into your square, and it never has a power.
var2: Other powers: sometimes only the jack is a blind swap and the queen lets you look first, or every king is “look and swap”. Some groups play without any powers for jacks and queens.
var3: Red king: in some groups it is worth −2, in others just 1 point like an ace. Some play without jokers.
var4: Penalty for a bad call: if the caller doesn't have the lowest total, they get extra points, often +10 or +25. In return the round winner sometimes scores 0.
var5: Stacking: some tables only allow stacking your own cards, or leave it out completely. Then the game is calmer and more about memory.
var6: Six cards: with 2 players or for a longer round, deal 6 cards in two rows of three and peek at three of them.
faq1q: Can I look at my cards again later?
faq1a: Only with a power: a 7 or 8 that you draw and throw away lets you peek at one of your own cards. Otherwise you have to remember.
faq2q: Does a power count if I swap the card out?
faq2a: No. Only a card that comes straight from the draw pile onto the discard pile has a power. A 7 you swap out of your square does nothing.
faq3q: Can I stack when it's not my turn?
faq3a: Yes, at any time, as long as the matching card is on top of the discard pile. You can stack your own cards and other players' cards.
faq4q: What if two players stack at the same time?
faq4a: Only the faster one counts. The slower one takes their card back. Strict groups add a penalty card for the slower player too.
faq5q: Can I move my cards around?
faq5a: No. Each card keeps its spot, otherwise nobody can keep track. Moving your cards costs a penalty card.
faq6q: What happens if I run out of cards?
faq6a: You stay in the round with 0 points and can still stack other players' cards – you just have nothing to give in return.
faq7q: Can I call Cambio right at the start?
faq7a: Yes, at the start of any of your turns. Early calls are bold, because you only know two of your cards.
faq8q: What's the difference between Cambio and Cabo?
faq8a: They are close relatives. Cabo is sold with its own cards from 0 to 13; Cambio is played with a normal deck, the red king as the best card and usually with stacking.
